podcast-dannyjones-YdO2e8TBOmQ:
Iya Whiteley, a space psychologist who has worked with NASA, joins Danny Jones for a talk on the minds of astronauts. The episode title asks what crews really see in high orbit. Whiteley studies how space flight strains and changes the people who fly.

Whiteley explains the stress, awe, and strange sights that crews report far above Earth. She also talks about how training tries to keep minds steady on long trips. Jones asks what a trip to Mars would demand of a crew's mental health. Listeners get a rare look at the human side of space flight, told by a pro who trains the flyers.
podcast-dannyjones-qNZgQly_vMQ:
Former soldier Jon Truett talks with Danny Jones about elite units and future war. Truett's path ran from roofing work to the parachute regiment. His brother's service first drew him toward the army.

The title points to his time linked to 22 SAS, Britain's famed special force. Talk turns to DARPA, the United States research arm for new war tools. They discuss body tech and the idea of super soldiers. The episode blends a personal enlistment story with hard questions about how far armies will push the human body. Truett speaks with care about that world.
podcast-tuckercarlson-h_GGl7poZMQ:
Tucker Carlson steps in as host of The Charlie Kirk Show in this episode, a passing of the torch between generations. Carlson, the elder statesman of the movement, takes the younger firebrand's chair. The swap itself is the story, two eras of the right in one seat.

Hosting Kirk's show, Carlson speaks to the young audience Kirk built on campuses and online. He shares his view of where their shared movement stands and what it must do next. The episode plays as both tribute and instruction. Young and faithful viewers get the mentor addressing the students in their own house.
